title: Shaft Seal Identifier
description: Explore FanPedia's seven shaft seal types, in three families, each with a reference infobox and a schematic cross-section; then classify twelve shuffled cards (parts, materials or order-line names) into the seven bins with two attempts each. The correct bin's infobox opens after every answer; mastery is 10 of 12 on the first attempt.

educational.audience: Adult professional development: new application engineers, sales staff, representatives and facilities staff
educational.topic: Identifying FanPedia's seven shaft seal types
learningObjectives: The learner will classify a fan shaft seal into one of seven FanPedia seal types from a description of its parts, materials or order-line name, with at least 10 of 12 correct on the first attempt.

accessibility.notes: describe() text (fallback mode); verdicts, infoboxes and the summary are announced through FP.announce (aria-live); ✓/✗ glyphs and solid/dashed borders pair with colour, and a wrong first pick gets a dashed outline; each bin button's aria-label says whether it opens the infobox or commits the card; keys 1-7 press a bin, Enter starts the quiz and goes on.

rules: Each card has exactly one correct bin.
A card is committed by pressing a bin; a wrong first attempt allows one more commit; score counts first-attempt correct answers only.
12 cards, shuffled, two attempts each; after each answer the correct bin's infobox opens.
Mastery is 10 of 12 on the first attempt; the mastery message reads 'You can identify FanPedia's seven shaft seal types from their parts.'
assumptions: Seven seal types in three families: contact (friction, V-ring, lip), carbon ring (single, double), stuffing box (plain, with gas purge).
limitations: Cross-sections are schematic and not to scale; exact construction varies by seal vendor.

sources: FanPedia (Twin City Fan, 2021), Shaft Seals pp. 149-155
Card wording written for Chapter 16 from those pages

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Explore the seven types with cross-sections, then classify unfamiliar descriptions with committed answers; feedback names the identifying part and opens the reference infobox.
keyQuestions: Is there a lantern ring and a purge hole?
commonMisconceptions: Any seal with a purge is a carbon ring seal.
A lip shaft seal and a bearing lip seal are the same part.
Single and double carbon ring seals differ only in size.
assessmentOpportunities: First-attempt score shown as 'First-attempt score: n of 12'; mastery is 10 of 12 on the first attempt; running line 'First-try correct: n of 12'.
